The data looks at the motivation behind an upward trend of church attendance by young adults: about one in three (34%) say they’re attending church more often than one year ago. Nearly half (45%) report no change. Attendance increases are highest among young men at 41 percent, Black young adults at 41 percent and Hispanic young adults at 36 percent. About one in five (21%) young adults say they are attending less often.

The findings cover the first two installments of a three-part series on what young adults want from church, part of Gloo’s ongoing State of the Church initiative. Taken together, the two installments suggest that reaching the next generation may depend less on reinventing the church experience than on the practices churches already have.

“Young people are showing up to talk to God, next to their people,” said Brianne Shaw, Director of Marketing and Church Spokesperson at Gloo. “For church leaders, that raises some practical questions: How easy is it for someone new to find someone to pray with? And will someone notice when they’re missing?”

Part one, “What Young Adults Are Looking for Spiritually at Church,” and part two, “The Social Reasons Why Young Adults Go to Church,” are available now. Part three publishes next week. Learn more about the 2026 State of the Church initiative at gloo.com/stateofthechurch.
